summary: Line and method-count limits are weak proxies for semantic complexity and can fragment cohesive logic into a navigation-heavy graph.

points.text: Mechanical splitting can replace one long unit with many thin wrappers, indirection and hidden coupling, increasing the total context required to understand behavior.
Declarative schemas, parsers, generated clients and test tables can be long yet conceptually simple; uniform caps create suppressions and churn without reducing risk.
Fault and change correlations may reflect difficult domains causing both large classes and defects, so reducing size alone may not improve the underlying design.
Aggressive public-method limits can force premature abstractions and expose more types, files and dependencies than a cohesive module requires.
